project.title: Nonlinear Generalized Monotonicity and Error Bounds for Proximal Point Convergence at Multivalued Graph Junctions

contract.gap: Quadratic generalized-monotonicity estimates need not control the non-Lipschitz proximal geometry generated by a multivalued graph near a branch junction.
contract.task: Combine nonlinear RL generalized monotonicity with an independent generalized error bound to obtain local PPA convergence, and identify a complete multivalued graph on which the nonlinear order is optimal.
outcomes: a selected-transition convergence theorem with a graph-level RL corollary
a direct gauge-composition convergence certificate with the sharp step denominator 2
a complete square-root seam with optimal exponent and exact orbit

questions.text: When do nonlinear RL generalized monotonicity and generalized metric subregularity imply local convergence of the PPA?
Can the theory certify a complete multivalued graph whose proximal geometry has optimal Holder order below one and violates every finite quadratic J-side estimate?

contract.contribution: A quantitative RLEB convergence mechanism that separates graph-level RL from the weaker geometry needed along selected proximal transitions, gives an explicit step-based compatibility test, and treats a complete multivalued seam attaining the nonlinear order.
nonclaims: RL with gamma=1 is not a new operator class.
Holder inverse regularity and high-order metric subregularity are not introduced here.
The scalar certificates are sufficient and are not claimed necessary for PPA convergence.
No global priority claim is made for general high-order inverse machinery.

semantic_locks.canonical: lambda<a,b> >= (||a+lambda b||^2-L^2||a+lambda b||^(2 gamma))/4 on all pairs of the relevant graph block
the convergence theorem may use the weaker solution-comparison J-side energy inequality for each selected proximal transition; this is not the definition of graph-level RL
RL solution comparison -> step bound -> residual at the output -> gauge composition -> distance contraction -> finite length and localization
lambda m > L/2 for the step-based critical certificate; lambda m > L/sqrt(2) for the energy certificate
best RL exponent 1/2, residual coefficient 1/4, distance-to-set factor 1/4, pointwise asymptotic factor 1/2

alignment.method: standard local range coverage, graph-level RL, step bound, output residual, generalized error bound, finite-length localization
alignment.evidence: main convergence theorem and power-law corollaries
alignment.result: local well-posed orbit and convergence to a point of the solution set
alignment.interpretation: nonquadratic proximal geometry can be compensated by sufficiently strong residual growth
alignment.limitation: coverage and error-bound certificates remain independent assumptions
alignment.contribution: direct gauge-composition theorem and complementary energy certificate

alignment.method: explicit proximal-mapping calculation, cross-branch J-side estimates, and an independent residual error bound
alignment.evidence: optimal-order seam theorem and exact orbit
alignment.result: complete proximal relation with optimal Holder exponent 1/2 and exact convergent orbit
alignment.interpretation: the nonlinear order is genuine and excludes finite quadratic J-side bounds on the same neighborhood
alignment.limitation: the explicit example has a multivalued operator but a single-valued proximal mapping; the selected-transition theorem covers the broader multivalued-proximal case under its stated assumptions
alignment.contribution: strict separation example and a precise account of the multivalued scope

decisions.decision: Restore the author's direct step-bound proof as the main narrative.
Retain the energy branch as a complementary certificate.
Keep the square-root seam as the flagship example.
Use inner-product RL and J-side energy throughout the main narrative.
Move the detailed signed-Schur verifier to an appendix unless an application without a closed proximal-mapping formula requires it in the main text.
Adopt the Luke--Tam style local range-coverage interface in the main assumption block and move selection-uniform transition geometry to a corollary.

issues.text: The general error-bound gauge is not yet illustrated by a genuinely nonpower orbit example.
The global priority of the signed-Schur verification assembly remains to be audited against the closest seam and active-set literature.
